title: Is this really the Premier League's 'Bermuda Triangle'?
description: Do the stats back the social media meme that Bournemouth, Brighton and Brentford form a Premier League 'Bermuda Triangle' where teams lose points?
fullText:
It's the place where points are lost and never to be seen again, according to a popular social media meme.

Draw a line from Brighton to Bournemouth to Brentford and back down to Brighton again and you will have formed the Premier League's very own "Bermuda Triangle".

Those three clubs have developed a reputation for taking points off the traditional Big Six - Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham.

Recent results have only fuelled the narrative and helped to push the tongue-in-cheek theory.

On Friday night, Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0. Less than 24 hours later, Brighton outclassed champions Arsenal, albeit by the same scoreline - though it was a victory that could arguably have been even more emphatic had David Raya not produced a couple of smart saves.

Bournemouth, meanwhile, pushed Liverpool all the way before falling to a gritty 1-0 defeat, with Alisson forced into a brilliant recovery stop to deny the Cherries an early opener.

Those are the sort of performances that stick in supporters' minds and help explain why the theory has taken hold.

Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Brighton have been the best-performing non-traditional Big Six side against Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Man City, Manchester United and Spurs, taking 42 points from 26 games - an average of 1.62 points per match.

The Cherries are not far behind, collecting 35 points from 26 matches, or 1.35 points per game.

Brentford, however, have taken 22 points from 26 matches, averaging 0.85 points per game. Newcastle (1.46), Nottingham Forest (1.46) and Aston Villa (1.38) have all matched or outperformed the Bees against the traditional Big Six over the same period.

In other words, the clubs most commonly grouped together by the meme have produced very different levels of success against elite opposition.

Brighton and Bournemouth have consistently taken points off the Premier League's heavyweights. Brentford's record is less convincing.

In fact, the Opta data suggests Brighton are the main reason the theory has gained such traction.

Since Fabian Hurzeler took charge, only Kenny Dalglish's Blackburn have recorded a better points-per-game return against the traditional Big Six among managers of non-Big-Six clubs with at least 10 matches.

The popularity of the Bermuda Triangle idea may say as much about perception as results.

When it comes to recruitment and spending, Bournemouth, Brighton and Brentford operate in a different world to the Premier League's biggest clubs. They cannot simply outspend Arsenal, Liverpool or Manchester City.

That makes their victories more memorable. Upsets also tend to linger longer in the memory because they fit a familiar story: well-run clubs outperforming opponents with significantly greater resources.

The meme is not entirely without foundation, although the evidence is considerably stronger for Brighton and Bournemouth than it is for Brentford.

Brentford's overall record is weaker, although a series of eye-catching victories under Thomas Frank and now Keith Andrews have helped cement their reputation as a difficult opponent for elite clubs. And the start to this season has helped: their Chelsea success added to by an opening day 3-0 rout of Spurs.

But the numbers do not support a three-club phenomenon quite as clearly as social media might suggest.

If there is a Premier League Bermuda Triangle, Brighton sit firmly at its centre.

The Seagulls' record against the traditional Big Six is not merely impressive by modern standards. According to Opta, it is one of the best any non-Big-Six club has produced in the Premier League era.

The only catch is that the evidence points less to a triangle and more to one standout club, with Bournemouth providing strong support and Brentford helping to supply some of the moments that keep the theory alive.

title: Arsenal early Premier League favourites – players to watch
description: Well, it had to happen didn’t it. No sooner were the pundits, bookies, and football fans in general, talking about Arsenal potentially going unbeaten this season and bringing back a new and updated ...
fullText:
Well, it had to happen didn't it. No sooner were the pundits, bookies, and football fans in general, talking about Arsenal potentially going unbeaten this season and bringing back a new and updated version of the 'Arsenal Invincibles', they go and get destroyed 3-0 by Brighton.

Fans of Premier League football are in for a long few weeks now, as we find ourselves gearing up for the first international break of the season. After a dismal display last weekend however, Arsenal fans will likely welcome this break as it will give them a chance to regroup, and will allow key players a chance to shine for their countries.

Despite such a poor showing against Brighton, The Gunners are still in a very strong position, and despite slipping to 2nd in the table, they're still strong contenders for another title. In fact, they are still favourites amongst most bookmakers, and when you look at the calibre of their players, it's easy to see why.

Arsenal Players to Watch this Season

With odds of 1/1 with both BOYLE Sports and Ladbrokes, the bookmakers clearly still have faith in The Gunners for the rest of the season.

But which players could prove instrumental in Arsenal's title defence this season? Let's take a look, shall we?

Since joining Arsenal, proficient German forward/attacking midfielder Kai Havertz has had a somewhat frustrating time, due largely to injuries.

Last season, the German netted 7 goals from 24 appearances. Compare that with the season before it, where he scored 15 goals from 36 appearances, and you can understand his frustration. Despite suffering injuries, he was still able to find the net on big occasions. He scored for The Gunners against PSG in the Champions League final, becoming the first ever German to score in two Champions League finals. He also scored in the Community Shield final, when Arteta's team defeated Man City 3-0.

As the German now returns to fitness, his precision passing, coupled with his two-footed ability, mean he'll certainly be one to watch this season. With 2 Premier League goals from 5 matches, he also looks set to better last season.

Another player who has been instrumental in Arsenal's title hopes has been England international, Bukayo Saka.

Currently, Saka has netted 3 times for The Gunners out of 5 appearances, which has hopefully answered any questions that people may have had regarding his fitness following injury.

Saka is a real handful for defenders due to his pace and accuracy. When he's not slotting goals in, he's usually whipping them into the box, as we saw for England during the World Cup, particularly during the Mexico game.

Saka is a Gunner through and through. A product of their youth academy, he's a testament to grass-roots football and emphasises everything there is to know and love about the beautiful game. It's clear he loves playing for his team, and it shows each time he steps on the pitch.

Although his last two seasons have been subdued by his standards, he's on course to regain that infamous form of 2023/24, which almost secured them the title.

The current Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard is another player to watch closely this season, for obvious reasons.

Odegaard, who captains both Arsenal, and his beloved home country of Norway, is a real playmaker of a midfielder. Despite questions being raised over his role in the club, he's gradually silenced his critics thanks to 2 goals from 5 games in the Prem.

Does he score the most goals? No, but he's about so much more than that. His passing is pin-point accurate, he's racked up plenty of assists, and as he regains his form following injury, his linking up with Saka and Havertz is going to be crucial if The Gunners want to make it two on the bounce.

If there's one plater that shone for England during the World Cup, that was not named Kane or Bellingham, it was Declan Rice. Despite dealing with a nagging injury (this seems to be a common theme for Arsenal) he was still able to put in some incredible balls and help England to reach the semis.

Last season, many believe he was largely responsible for Arsenal securing the title, and honesty, it's hard to argue with that assessment. A set-piece specialist through and through, Arteta's squad looked absolutely lethal during set-pieces, and Rice's balls being whipped into the box (stop laughing, we're all adults here) were the reason why. It wasn't always the most exciting style of play, but it helped them end the drought.

Rice currently has 2 assists to his name, though you can rest assured that come Spring, that number will be much higher.

title: Charles taking record-breaking price tag in his stride
description: Fulham midfielder Shea Charles tells BBC Sport NI he does "not really think about" the price tag which saw him become Northern Ireland's most expensive footballer when he joined Premier League Fulham from Southampton.
fullText:
If Shea Charles is feeling a weight of expectation from being the most expensive Northern Ireland footballer ever his demeanour does not betray it.

Interviewed by BBC Sport NI before the forthcoming four-game Nations League bonanza, the Fulham midfielder cuts a laid-back but determined figure who is keen to play a key part in helping a young Northern Ireland side continue to build on recent progress.

Charles' record-breaking £30m move from Championship side Southampton to the Cottagers in the summer gave him the opportunity to move up a division and ply his trade in the Premier League.

He describes becoming NI's most expensive footballer as "quite crazy".

"I think I was like second or third before that. But to be number one, it's really cool. Just to be in the Premier League and just being able to play my football is amazing," he told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

"For me, I don't really think about it [the price tag] too much, and you see what a lot of people are going for these days, it's kind of crazy.

"I've just got really good people around me, living with my younger brother and my older brother, mum and dad. I've got a really good friendship group that keep me grounded."

International football, rather than the club game, will occupy the 22-year-old's attention over the coming weeks as Michael O'Neill's side face Georgia home and away, Hungary and Ukraine over the coming weeks.

Already capped 35 times since making his debut in June 2022, Charles emphasises the influence international football has had on advancing his career prospects and improving his game.

"International football has always been massive for me ever since I made my debut – the types of players you play against, the teams you are playing, you rarely got to play against them when you're playing in the Championship.

"Being able to show your level against those kind of players was always going to help.

"I feel like he [O'Neill] has really trusted me from the moment that I came in, starting me in any game that he could really, and I'm obviously very thankful for that.

"I feel like Michael has given me a bit of responsibility, especially taking the armband a couple of times, so I just try to set an example, whether that's on the pitch or off the pitch, and just be someone the young lads can look up to."

Charles has played a part in all five of Fulham's Premier League matches this season, starting in three of those, including draws against Liverpool and Manchester United in recent weeks.

Alvaro Arbeloa's side sit 19th in the table, with two draws and three defeats to date.

"Whether it was with Southampton or by getting a move the aim was always to get back to the Premier League.

"It's really exciting and I've settled in really well. It's a really good club and when I spoke to the manager we saw football in the same way.

"Against Man United it was a really good game and I thought we were unlucky not to win the game. To play in a game like that so early after my move was really good."

His brother, goalkeeper Pierce, currently on loan at Queen's Park Rangers from Manchester City after a summer switch, is also an integral part of the Northern Ireland squad.

"It's kind of the stuff of dreams to play with your brother on the international stage. When you're playing teams like France and Italy and he's playing alongside you it's really cool.

"We're really close, we played football together when we were younger, we've always been best mates."

English-born Charles qualifies to play for Northern Ireland through his mother, who follows the careers of her sons avidly.

"She is dead proud, you can see on her face when you see her in the crowd at Windsor Park in particular.

"I can tell how proud she is of us and for us both to be playing together is just incredible.

"I can't remember the last one she has missed at Windsor Park. She is there all the time. She was in Italy and she tries to get to as many away games as possible.

"I told her that when I was younger [that I would play for Northern Ireland], me and Pierce, and I've definitely followed through with that promise."

Charles feels the "potential is definitely there" for the squad "to prove how good we are".

"It's a really tight-knit group, everyone gets along. Whenever any new boys come in I always feel like they fit in so well.

"When you get the likes of Ceadach [O'Neill] and Braiden [Graham] coming in you begin to feel that little bit older. It's a really good group."

title: Max Dowman handed England senior squad verdict as Arsenal star eyes record
description: Arsenal's Max Dowman has been tipped to make his England debut in the near future, but the youngest player in Premier League history has been told he must progress through the U21s before earning a senior call-up
fullText:
Arsenal prodigy Max Dowman has been informed that a direct call-up to the senior England squad is not on the immediate horizon, with the U21s identified as his logical next step.

The 16-year-old, who etched his name in the history books as the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer last season, has experienced a meteoric rise and is now generating serious discussion about a senior Three Lions berth. He has been on Thomas Tuchel's radar since before the World Cup, but is set to feature with the U19s on Friday.

U21s manager Lee Carsley could find himself welcoming a number of promoted players following the withdrawal of five squad members, including Declan Rice and Cole Palmer, from the senior England setup, which faces four fixtures over the next 10 days, beginning with Spain on Saturday.

However, Carsley has made his position abundantly clear — Dowman's progression will almost certainly run through the U21s rather than the senior squad, as coaching staff look to safeguard his development through a measured pathway they believe will underpin a lengthy international career.

He said, via The Mirror: "It's important players develop at their own pace. Max is an outstanding talent, the timing and the balance of when he comes to the Under-21s is inevitable.

"He's going to the U21s because of his talent, but we have to make sure we do that at the right time. We have to be patient and make sure that ultimately we want them to play for the senior team for a prolonged period. So we have to make sure that we get the time right with that. We had a similar issue a few years ago with Ethan Nwaneri."

Carsley emphasized: "Thomas and I speak regularly about squad selection and obviously Max is always in the conversation because of his talent."

title: Summer signings assessed & why Town fans can have hope
description: Heading into the international break, Ipswich Town have double the amount of points at this stage of the season compared with their previous Premier League campaign.  Bear in mind as well that they've played four teams who are featuring in Europe this season.  Saturday at Hill Dickinson Stadium - against a team with just their domestic fixtures to worry about - was particularly frustrating, as Gary O'Neil's side didn't deserve to come away with nothing.
fullText:
Heading into the international break, Ipswich Town have double the amount of points at this stage of the season compared with their previous Premier League campaign.

However, I can't help but feel slightly disappointed. While I probably would have taken a tally of six from the opening five matches when the fixtures were announced in June, Town's efforts have, in my opinion, warranted more.

Bear in mind as well that they've played four teams who are featuring in Europe this season.

Saturday at Hill Dickinson Stadium - against a team with just their domestic fixtures to worry about - was particularly frustrating, as Gary O'Neil's side didn't deserve to come away with nothing.

The fact that they did - and will also be without Abdul Fatawu next time because of a daft suspension - leaves a bit of a sour taste.

Let's focus on some of the positives from that afternoon on Merseyside though, beginning in goal, where Christian Walton justified the manager's big call in making a change between the posts.

I was perhaps among the minority in thinking that four games in might be too soon to drop Kjell Scherpen, but Walton looked assured and composed, just as he did when he took a similar chance last season.

He appears to have solved Town's goalkeeping conundrum with little fuss, and deserves to now be given an extended chance in the top-flight. Oh, and there was very little he could have done about Everton's somewhat freak winning goal.

Player of the match Abdoul Ouattara is another that deserves more than a mention.

The 20-year-old, making his first Premier League start, was outstanding at right-back, and justified another big call from the manager in choosing the Ivorian over the more experienced Darnell Furlong, who was so impressive during last season's run to promotion.

Town's plethora of summer arrivals have, in general, given supporters real hope that their latest Premier League stay will be an extended one.

Issa Diop has complemented Jacob Greaves or Dara O'Shea very well at centre-back, while Exequiel Palacios and Sasa Lukic are undoubtedly an upgrade on the midfield starters of two years ago .

That said, they have a long way to go before achieving the club legendary status of Sam Morsy and Massimo Luongo.

In Julio Encisio, Town have a player who can turn a game in an instant, but the surprise package for me has been Emersonn in the number nine role.

I hadn't been expecting a huge amount from the Brazil striker during the early stages of his first spell in English football but, to his credit, he has already become a fixture in the side.

The former Toulouse player has a couple of goals to his name already, and his hold-up play has been very impressive.

With that in mind, it is no surprise that Zian Flemming is still waiting for a first league start in his new club colours, but the Dutchman will be needed further down the line.

He has shown from his cameos so far that he will be ready to take any chance that comes his way.

In summary, O'Neil and his players have given themselves a very good platform from which to kick on, and Town supporters will be relishing the return of domestic football after the internationals, rather than fearing it.

title: How Premier League teams have really started - according to xG
description: Which Premier League teams have overperformed their xG and who has underperformed?
fullText:
How have Premier League teams really started?

At this stage last season Liverpool were top, with five wins out of five, and Tottenham were third. Given that they finished fifth and 17th respectively, it shows that the table shouldn't be taken too seriously this early on.

While any statistics should be taken with a pinch of salt - given such a small sample size of games and the fact that some teams have had more difficult starts than others - they do provide a more accurate picture of how the season could unfold.

Expected goals (xG) tells us how much teams have dominated games, based on the number and quality of shots they've taken and faced. Basically, how well they've performed in general before finishing, shot-stopping and plain old luck come into play.

And Premier League history shows us that the more a team dominates games, the more points they win in the long run.

It's best to exclude penalties as refereeing decisions and defensive clumsiness give a false impression of how good teams actually are at attacking and defending, especially at this early stage.

Champions Arsenal may have suffered their biggest defeat in three years last weekend at Brighton but they've still been the best team overall based on xG difference.

Leaders Manchester City are not too far behind them in terms of how much they've dominated their games, while there's nothing fortunate about unbeaten Brentford's impressive start to the season.

Manchester United constantly seem to flip between feast and famine, when often they've simply been fine. Despite their underwhelming start, only three teams have a higher xG difference so far.

The likes of Nottingham Forest and Bournemouth have also been better than their position in the early table suggests.

At the other end, Aston Villa, Crystal Palace and Newcastle have been the least impressive in terms of their overall performance, with the latter perhaps the most surprising given their position in the top half.

It's still early days, so there's no need to panic just yet, but it shows that those teams have a lot of room to improve - something Villa did to great effect after a slow start last season by finishing fourth.

Worryingly for the established sides though, the promoted teams seem like they won't be going down without a fight, with both Hull and Ipswich making genuinely solid starts to the campaign.

Looking at teams' numbers going forward, Brighton have the best attack so far based on the number and quality of chances they've had, followed by Manchester City, Brentford and Manchester United.

Although the Gunners are more admired for their defensive prowess, it's still surprising that eight teams have a higher xG than champions Arsenal, while Liverpool and Chelsea also rank in mid-table.

Brighton not only have the highest xG but have also been one of the most ruthless sides in front of goal, scoring 15 non-penalty goals from their 10.7 xG.

The only team to be more clinical than the Seagulls is their avian cousins the Magpies, who actually have the lowest xG in the league so far.

Newcastle have scored twice as many goals as a team historically would given the chances they've had - 9 goals from 4.5 xG - but head coach Matthias Jaissle will no doubt want his team to create more and not have to rely on such sharp finishing as the season goes on.

In contrast, Coventry, Sunderland, Nottingham Forest and Tottenham have all scored three goals fewer than they really should have given the opportunities they've had in their first five games.

It'll be interesting to see whether those teams genuinely have a problem with their finishing or if their luck in front of goal simply begins to change in the games to come.

As mentioned earlier, champions Arsenal are renowned for their defence and they still have by far the best backline in the league - even taking their heavy defeat by Brighton into account.

While Forest head coach Oliver Glasner has work to do to get his side scoring goals, he's already instilled a solid foundation to build from at the back, as has Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

There's a lot of construction work needed in the capital as Crystal Palace, Fulham and Chelsea have all been far too open at the back so far this season, although Xabi Alonso's side are not quite as terrible as the 12 goals they've conceded suggests.

Brighton's brilliance going forward has come at the cost of them not being particularly solid in defence, with Fabian Hurzeler's team perhaps a little fortunate not to have conceded more often.

Everton and Leeds have also conceded three goals fewer than expected given the chances they've faced, although both sides have been among the strongest defensively overall.

Just five games into the new campaign, it's too early to be making any concrete claims about how sides will perform but their underlying numbers have given us a glimpse of what might be in store this season.

title: Arteta agrees new deal with champions Arsenal
description: Mikel Arteta agrees an improved new contract with Premier League champions Arsenal.
fullText:
Mikel Arteta has agreed an improved new contract with Premier League champions Arsenal.

The Spaniard's current deal expires at the end of this season but talks over a new contract have been ongoing for a number of months.

BBC Sport reported earlier this month that an agreement between all parties was close.

And it is now understood Arteta has reached a final agreement with the Gunners to extend his stay.

There is no confirmation over the length of his new contract but it is set to take him into at least his 10th year at the club following his arrival in December 2019.

The new contract will also include a sharp pay increase from his current salary of £10m per year plus an additional £5m in bonuses.

Speaking about his contract talks, Arteta said last week that fans did not need to "worry" because he wanted to stay.

"I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with," he said.

News of Arteta's agreement over a new deal at Arsenal won't come as a shock - but it is a major development nevertheless.

The fact his existing deal expires at the end of the season did put a slightly greater emphasis on the speed of discussions than normal.

But Arteta has been transparent about his desire to stay at the club beyond the end of this campaign.

Dynasty building is what has driven Arteta's decision. Winning Arsenal's first Premier League title in 20 years last season is viewed as just the start.

Coming within a penalty kick of winning their first Champions League trophy came as a gut-wrenching blow - but also a huge motivation.

With that in mind, there was never a sense Arteta was preparing to walk away from the team he has built to become one of the best in European football.

So with a deal for their manager to stay now agreed, the foundation of Arsenal's recent revitalisation into a footballing force remains in place.

Does more history beckon? Arteta is committed to finding out.

title: Egan's late career resurgence back to Premier League
description: BBC Sport NI looks at Republic of Ireland centre-back's John Egan's rise back to the Premier League with Hull City and the international set-up under Heimir Hallgrimsson.
fullText:
Just 18 months ago a 31-year-old John Egan was struggling for minutes off the bench for promotion-chasing Burnley and decided to make a January switch to fellow Championship side Hull City.

Fast forward to the present day and Egan is a Premier League regular for the Tigers, who have taken everyone by surprise upon their return to the top flight.

It's been quite a turnaround for the now 33-year-old, who probably thought his last Premier League appearance had already come, when he was taken off on a stretcher with a season-ending Achilles injury when playing for Sheffield United against West Ham in September 2023.

Egan has quietly rebuilt his career after being released by the Blades, first with the Clarets before finding a home at Hull after joining in 2024.

He signed a new two-year deal earlier this month, has played five of their league games and has even forced his way back into the Republic of Ireland squad.

His late career resurgence back to the Premier League is a story of perseverance and unwavering belief despite considerable adversity.

Hallgrimsson spoke to players individually about Israel games

Coleman not included in Republic of Ireland squad

Egan made 208 appearances for Sheffield United during his six seasons with the club, winning promotion to the Premier League with them in 2019 and 2023.

He was named club captain in the summer of 2023, but would play his last game for the Blades in September that same year as an Achilles injury curtailed his Premier League return and kept him out for close to 10 months.

The defender's contract expired the following summer and the club decided not to renew the deal, leaving Egan hurt and in the lurch as he tried to battle back from that serious injury and continue his career.

He went on trial to Burnley and West Ham, with then Clarets boss Scott Parker seeing enough from the experienced centre-back to offer him a one-year deal with the club seeking a quick return to the top flight after relegation the previous season.

With Burnley then getting off to a flying start in the Championship, Egan, who was working back to full fitness, was restricted to just seven appearances and decided to swap a promotion push at Turf Moor for a relegation battle with Hull just five months later.

He signed an 18-month deal and was thrown straight in, completing his first 90 minutes in over a year, coincidentally against Burnley in a 2-0 loss in February.

The Kerry native would go on to make 10 more appearances as Hull stayed up on goal difference on the final day.

Manager Sergej Jakirovic then came in and transformed the club the following campaign, with a fully-fit Egan a key player in their success.

He played 48 times as Hull sneaked into the play-offs and then beat Middlesborough in the final to return to the Premier League for the first time since 2017.

Egan picked up where he left off last season in the top flight this term, as evidenced by his performance in the opening day 2-0 victory over Manchester United.

He made 18 clearances against the Red Devils and has since helped the Tigers keep clean sheets against Coventry and Aston Villa before they earned a point against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge and lost narrowly against Newcastle.

It's been a dream return to the top flight for Hull and Egan, who have shown they are up for the fight in the battle to stay in the league.

Egan's form at Hull helped him to earn an international recall with the Republic of Ireland in October last year, after two years without a call-up.

Previously an automatic starter, the rise of the likes of Nathan Collins, Dara O'Shea and Jake O'Brien have pushed him down the pecking order and he has played a bit-part role under Heimir Hallgrimsson.

Egan came off the bench for the closing stages of the 1-0 defeat against Portugal and was then on the bench for the subsequent wins against Armenia, Portugal and famously Hungary, which gave them a shot at the World Cup via the play-offs.

He again was an unused substitute in the heartbreaking shootout defeat against Czech Republic before winning his 38th cap by starting in a 0-0 friendly draw against North Macedonia in May.

With Hallgrimsson's preference for playing with three centre-backs, Egan has certainly staked a claim for occupying one of those slots in the Nations League opener against Kosovo given his start to the season.

His case is strengthened by the fact that captain Collins is out injured, O'Brien has been limited to three appearances for Everton and O'Shea has been playing out of position at right-back for Ipswich Town.

The other centre-back options in the squad - new call-up Liam Kitching, Jimmy Dunne and James Abankwah - are inexperienced on the international stage.

description: Arne Slot's time as Liverpool manager came to a bit of an abrupt end. Just a season after winning the Premier League title, the Dutchman was relieved of his duties due to the poor performances that hi...
fullText:

Just a season after winning the Premier League title, the Dutchman was relieved of his duties due to the poor performances that his men were putting in.

The Reds did a terrible job of trying to defend their top flight title as they only finished fifth in the league.

And, to make things worse, they only got to the round of 16 in the Champions League.

All of these things combined together to make fans believe that another massive rebuild was on its way to Anfield.

Four players ended up getting brought in during the summer but, since there are still a couple of glaring problems among their ranks, some more transfers are needed.

Of course, the January transfer window is still quite a few months away yet but, that hasn't stopped the rumour mill from turning.

When Trent Alexander-Arnold left Liverpool last summer, everyone knew that he would be difficult to replace.

The right-back was one of the Reds' most creative players and, even though Jeremie Frimpong was brought in to replace him, he has not managed to meet expectations.

fullText:
Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk insists he is "focusing on the "present" and there is "nothing to report" when it comes to his Anfield contract.

The 35-year-old's deal expires at the end of this season and it remains to be seen whether the centre-back, who joined Liverpool from Southampton in January 2018, will be offered an extension or he will choose to move on.

Van Dijk has played every minute of Liverpool's Premier League campaign so farand said his side have "not had a bad start" under new boss Andoni Iraola.

The Reds are unbeaten in seven games this season and go into the international break sixth in the table after two wins and three draws in the league.

Speaking after Sunday's 1-0 win at Bournemouth, Van Dijk said: "Any manager that comes to a new environment and a new club needs a bit of time, and the same goes with players.

"We work a lot, almost every day, and hopefully it works sooner rather than later. It is down to us to get results. At a club like Liverpool, you don't have a lot of time to get results so you have to get the points on the board.

"We've not had a bad start - we could have done better in a couple of games, but we are where we are. On to the next."

Van Dijk will now head off on international duty after holding positive talks about his Netherlands future with new manager Xavi, who was at Anfield to watch Liverpool's Champions League opener against Atletico Madrid earlier this month.

title: What have we learned from the Premier League so far?
description: BBC Sport takes a look at the opening weeks of the Premier League season as a long international break arrives.
fullText:
The Premier League takes a near three-week break as we enter a four-game international window.

So, what have we learned from the opening five matches of the season?

Premier League champions Arsenal were looking fairly unstoppable in the opening weeks of the season.

A win over Brighton on Saturday would have given the Gunners a club-record equalling eighth consecutive win in all competitions to start the season.

But that all ended with a 3-0 loss at Amex Stadium on Saturday.

The Gunners had not lost a league game by more than one goal, let alone three, since October 2024.

It was their heaviest defeat in the league since May 2023 when they lost 3-0 to the same opposition.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," said boss Mikel Arteta.

"What we've done, the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable - but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta

Many wondered if Manchester City would experience a post-Pep Guardiola slump when the legendary boss left after a decade.

Things did not start too well under Enzo Maresca, with the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

But they have won all five games in the Premier League - and seven in a row in all competitions - after Sunday's entertaining 5-3 win over Sunderland.

That takes them three points clear of Arsenal.

"In the press conference before the game, I said I expect a very tough game," said Maresca. "Then we also conceded two or three goals but we have learned a lot in these eight weeks and this is good."

Perfect 24 hours as Man City put pressure on Arsenal

Brighton and Brentford, two clubs who have never won a major trophy, have continued to impress this season.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton enjoyed that 3-0 win over Arsenal to see them sit third in the table, only two points behind the Gunners.

Brighton have won at home against the reigning Premier League champions in each of the last three seasons.

Star player Pascal Gross laughed and said "no" when BBC Sport asked him if Albion were in the title race.

But stranger things have happened...

Meanwhile, just one point below them in the table are Keith Andrews' Brentford.

Many tipped the Bees to struggle after the departure of Thomas Frank last summer but if anything they improved under their former set-piece coach Andrews.

And their start to this season - unbeaten after five games and fourth in the table - is showing he is no one-season wonder as a manager.

They go into the break on the back of their most impressive result, a 3-0 home win over Chelsea.

Leeds, impressing again under boss Daniel Farke, are also on nine points and in a potential Champions League place.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool and Everton are just below them on goal difference.

From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary in style

Seven years apart, United did the same thing twice hoping for different results - appointing a club legend who last managed in Britain in the Championship after a good start as caretaker boss.

In 2019 it was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and this time it was Michael Carrick.

But this season, after Carrick having a summer to work on his team, the Red Devils have only won once in the league.

Their five points after five league games is their joint fewest at this stage of a Premier League season.

They go into the international break on the back of a 1-1 draw against Fulham, and even needed a late deflected Matheus Cunha strike to stop the Cottagers winning their first game all season.

After the Lisandro Martinez own goal that give Fulham the lead, ex-United captain Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: "I've watched Manchester United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen.

"Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort."

United's owners will have almost three weeks to stew on this before they host fellow underachievers Tottenham (more on them soon) on 10 October.

In 2024 and 2025, the three promoted teams went straight back down - mostly with really low points tallies too.

But that streak came to an end last year when Sunderland finished seventh to qualify for Europe and Leeds came 14th. Only Burnley went down.

And the early weeks of this season indicate we could be in for a similar situation.

Hull City are eighth after five games, with their 2-1 loss to Newcastle their first defeat.

Ipswich are 11th. And Coventry, after losing the first four games without scoring, beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 and only sit in the drop zone on goal difference.

A Coventry win 25 years in the making

Tottenham finished 17th the last two seasons, their lowest two finishes since being in the second tier in 1977-78.

But expectations were raised after a summer of big spending - with Spurs splashing out £302m as well as making two high-profile loan signings.

Defence and midfield in particular were overhauled, with new wingers too.

But they are left with one senior striker in Dominic Solanke, who has only scored 12 Premier League goals in over two years at the club.

"I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle," said TNT pundit and ex-England international Joe Cole.

Saturday's 3-2 loss against Aston Villa sees them sit 19th going into the break - despite scoring their first two league goals of the campaign.

"We have to put on the pitch something more than we are putting," said manager Roberto de Zerbi.

"Football is tactical but it is blood, it is fighting, it is first one on the ball. We will suffer until the next game."

No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat

Many were keen to see what Xabi Alonso could do at Chelsea this season.

The Spaniard memorably led Bayer Leverkusen to a historic unbeaten German double in 2023-24.

And they made big changes to their squad this summer, with £117m attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers and new first-choice keeper Emiliano Martinez both coming in from Aston Villa.

There have been 22 goals in their five league games - more coming against them than for them - and they sit 10th.

And that is not even counting the 6-3 win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

Hugely entertaining for the neutrals - but perhaps not for Chelsea fans or management.

title: 🐈‍⬛ Brian Brobbey earns cult hero status with hat-trick vs Man City
description: Sunderland's recent resurgence as a force to be reckoned with in the Premier League has been one of the feel-good stories in the top flight of English football. Under Regis Le Bris, the club has becom...
fullText:
Sunderland's recent resurgence as a force to be reckoned with in the Premier League has been one of the feel-good stories in the top flight of English football.

Under Regis Le Bris, the club has become one of the toughest outfits to come up against, and with Brian Brobbey impressively leading the line, few will fancy 90 minutes against the Black Cats.

And against Manchester City this afternoon, the Dutch international and former Ajax standout is putting together a one-off performance to remember, one week after he made himself out to be a nuisance against Arsenal at the Stadium of Light.

In doing so, Brobbey now sits alongside a handful of memorable figures and one outright club icon, becoming just the fifth Sunderland player to score a Premier League hat-trick, joining Kevin Phillips (two), Darren Bent, Jermain Defoe, and Adam Johnson.

Brobbey is also the first player to hit City on three occasions in a single match since Jamie Vardy back in September 2020, signaling his arrival as a true goal threat in the league.

And with the transfer market now being the Wild West that it has become, Brobbey may well become the next big summer signing should this run of form continue.

title: Haaland completes Premier League set by scoring against Sunderland
description: Erling Haaland’s goal against Sunderland today means he has now scored against all 25 sides he has faced in the Premier League. Men's Team Haaland becomes top scorer in Manchester derbies in Premier...
fullText:
Erling Haaland's goal against Sunderland today means he has now scored against all 25 sides he has faced in the Premier League.

The Norwegian's 81st minute finish against the Black Cats at the Etihad Stadium was the final piece in the puzzle of the Premier League teams he's come up against in just over four years in England.

He's most enjoyed playing West Ham in the top-flight, with 11 strikes in just eight games with the Hammers.

10 goals have come against both Crystal Palace and Wolves, while he's now the leading scorer in Manchester derbies in the Premier League with nine goals.

Fulham, Everton and Brighton have all felt the force of Haaland's irrepressible hunger for goals too, while he's stood up in plenty of big games against regular title rivals Arsenal with six goals against them.

He's even managed to find the net against three teams – Sheffield United, Luton Town and Coventry – despite playing them just once in the competition.

It took him until his third meeting with Sunderland before finding the net however.

His latest strike takes him to five in the Premier League so far this season, putting him in the early lead for this year's Golden Boot.

He's already won that award in three of his first four campaigns at City, including a record-breaking haul of 36 in 2022/23.

In total, he has 117 goals in 137 Premier League appearances. Only 22 men have ever found the net 

Just last week he became the third highest scorer in our 132-year history, surpassing Tommy Johnson on 166.

He's now hot on the heels of Eric Brook, who found the net 177 times between 1928 and 1939, but still some way off Sergio Aguero's record of 260.

fullText:

Brian Brobbey hit a hat-trick for the visitors but ended up on the losing side, while Erling Haaland ending an unwanted statistic with a late goal.

Here's how I rated the players, and you can see how you scored them below.

title: Moyes demands more from Everton - but don't mention Europe
description: Fifth in the Premier League table and yet to lose this season, Everton are on the up, but boss David Moyes wants further improvements - and don't mention Europe.
fullText:
Unbeaten after five games and fifth in the Premier League, Everton boss David Moyes is refusing to think of Europe after allowing himself to dream last season.

"We are not using those words this year," said Moyes bluntly after a 1-0 victory at home against Ipswich Town took the Toffees to nine points.

They have two wins and three draws from their first month of the campaign, a healthy start.

But the way 2025-26 ended for Everton was a painful experience for Moyes and the club's fans, and nobody will be getting ahead of themselves this time.

A 3-0 win over Chelsea in March had left Moyes' side eighth, three points off what would have been a Champions League place.

But just as the fans dreamed of a first European experience since 2017-18, the wheels came off with no wins in their final seven games.

Everton finished 13th, four points behind Brighton, who qualified for the Conference League, and five off Sunderland, who joined Bournemouth and Crystal Palace in the Europa League.

So it is no wonder Moyes is refusing to get carried away now.

Asked whether he had challenged his players to earn European qualification this season, Moyes said: "Not [saying] in front of you people [the media], that's for sure, because we're still preparing ourselves and make sure we can do the best we can.

"I enjoyed saying the words last year. If you think of what we had done, been relegation material when we came in January [2025], got out and won the games, 12/13 new players had to come in...

"But the players had done so well, I started to believe that we had a real chance, and it allowed me to be like that."

Everton's strong start, in which they have also won two Carabao Cup games to set up a home last-16 tie against Newcastle in October, had been based on a solid defence.

Moyes' side have kept five clean sheets in seven matches overall and got the three points against Ipswich thanks to an 11th-minute goal from Thierno Barry, his fifth of the season.

What makes Everton's form even more impressive is the fact Barry is the only recognised striker at the club after Beto moved to Fiorentina on transfer deadline day, with key attacking midfielder Iliman Ndiaye joining Manchester City on the same day.

However, Moyes felt his side, one of only five still unbeaten in the Premier League, still have plenty of work to do before he will be happy.

"We've had draws at Tottenham and Bournemouth away from home and we've done pretty well," said Moyes. "Keeping clean sheets is something to be pleased about and try to build on.

"We've statistically been making more chances and we had 21 shots [against Ipswich], which is very good, but only two on target which isn't very good.

"The players get huge credit to get to this point, unbeaten in five games. It's really good, but I'm expecting them to do this.

"If we're thinking 'we're doing a great job because we've gone a few games', no, the manager expects that. I'm actually more disappointed that we aren't scoring more goals.

"I'm rapping them like you wouldn't believe - why are we not getting better crosses into the box, better finishes, shooting from the edge of the box, not scoring more? That's the only thing we're missing from being a half-decent side."

When Moyes returned for a second spell in charge of Everton in January 2025, the Toffees were 16th, one point clear of the relegation zone.

He has had to cope with rising expectations but was quick to point to the club's progress since he came back.

"I heard a lot of things [said] that last year was not so good and I thought 'my goodness, I don't know what the people are talking or writing about because it's absolute baloney'.

"It was fantastic what we did and we came so close to doing something that would have been incredibly special after no money, being on the verge of relegation, moving to a new stadium - and it has never been an easy job for anyone moving to a new stadium - so we came really close."

Assessing Everton's unbeaten status, former England midfielder and BBC pundit Danny Murphy said: "Nothing surprises me with a David Moyes side.

"They're so well organised, so well motivated and always dangerous when their backs are against the wall. There's been a lot of discontent among the fanbase regarding the owners and a transfer policy that left themselves short in forward areas.

"But the rest of the side is so well balanced, they all know their jobs, they know what they're doing and that backline with the keeper behind it is really solid. So, I never thought it was a catastrophe that they didn't get a striker in.

"Because they're so well organised and defensively so good, they're always going to nick results when they're not playing well. I do understand the fans' frustration, but I didn't think for a second they'd be in any danger because they didn't get cover in for their forwards.

"It is a thin squad, but they've still got quality."

Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford told BBC Sport the result felt like a positive way to end this part of the season, with the international break meaning the Toffees are not in league action again until 11 October when they will face Hull City.

"You have to dig in, that's the Everton way," Pickford said. "We are building momentum and we will be focused and ready to go when we come back. It was a great way to finish the week off."

Looking at the contribution of goalscorer Barry, who found the net just eight times last season but now looks a greater threat, Pickford said: "He works hard and the goals will come from working hard. The first year in the Premier League is always tough. He has found his feet and he has started a lot better this year.

"It's always good to finish with a win, especially before a long international break."

title: No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat
description: Tottenham look no closer to solving their problems as they slip to a home defeat by Aston Villa to add to their Premier League misery.
fullText:
The closer Tottenham went to scoring, the more it seemed likely they would concede.

"Too fragile" was how boss Roberto de Zerbi described his side after the 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa.

Comfortable and on top until Johan Manzambi's scrappy opener for the visitors - while Spurs were temporarily down to 10 men as Micky van de Ven had treatment - the home side never recovered.

It only got worse as goals from Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia put the visitors 3-0 up.

De Zerbi's men now go into a three-week international break still waiting for a first Premier League win this season as Conor Gallagher and Jan Paul van Hecke's late goals - the club's first in the league - were of little consolation.

In the bottom three after spending over £300m in the summer, there appears to be no end in sight to Spurs' struggles.

Tottenham have failed to win any of their past 36 Premier League matches when conceding first, so the writing was on the wall at half-time.

They dominated the opening 20 minutes and Villa keeper Zion Suzuki denied Savio and Archie Gray but, without a goal, Tottenham were always going to be vulnerable at the other end.

And so, in first-half injury time, a Villa goal was almost inevitable.

Andy Robertson tried to stop a corner but only gifted the ball to John McGinn and, after Boubacar Kamara's effort, Manzambi prodded in from close range. It added the insult to Van de Ven's injury, a blow to the face that kept him off the pitch.

Some Tottenham fans missed the goal as they headed for their half-time refreshments, but several thousand did not bother to stay until the end.

They streamed out of the stands after Buendia's brilliant 25-yard bullet found the top corner in the 79th minute, and that meant those fans missed Gallagher and Van Hecke's late efforts.

De Zerbi said: "My focus is why we concede the first goal with 10 players, we can stay stronger, communicate more and more, defend in a compact way.

"I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur as a centre-back in that minute and Mateus Fernandes as a midfielder. If we have a red card we can play 70 minutes with 10 players.

"In the second half we scored the goal with [Mohammed] Kudus, offside, I don't know if some players lost energy but we conceded an unacceptable goal. We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86% more long balls than last season.

"We had many meetings [about it] and we have to explain another game like Newcastle where we played the first half well and then we lose. It's my responsibility.

"I take my responsibility, but in that moment of the game we have to defend, we have to defend compact, the leaders have to be leaders.

"I am very sad and frustrated with the performance. We cannot lose this game in this way. The second goal we conceded was incredible."

"Sacked in the morning" chanted the Villa fans to De Zerbi who, at times, looked out of ideas once his side fell 2-0 behind.

It was Tottenham's worst start to a top-flight season since 2008-09, when they also had two points after five games.

Juande Ramos was dismissed as manager after three more defeats before Harry Redknapp lifted them up to eighth. Spurs have also now gone five league games without a win at the start of a season for the first time since 1986.

Former Brighton striker Glenn Murray, however, says De Zerbi needs time.

"He is trying to build something, it will take time," he told BBC's Final Score. "Taking the emotion out of it, looking at the stats, they have had more shots in three of the past four games, more possession and more touches in the opposition box.

"They are positives, be patient, the metrics are there to say he will turn it around. They need to be patient with Roberto de Zerbi, with all the signings, it takes time to gel and get to know each other."

A decisive moment came when Kudus thought he had levelled on the hour, but Robertson was ruled just offside having delivered the cross. Seven minutes later Jackson scored from Suzuki's long launch downfield and it was game over.

Villa's rebuild, the club committing to spending more than £250m, was out of necessity because of their own high-profile exits.

There was an expectation change was forthcoming and the Europa League winners were always going to go through a period of transition.

But a first league victory was vital for them too after three defeats in their opening four games.

While Villa look in better shape as new players settle, Spurs have thrown money at their problems after two relegation battles, but they are no closer to solving them. They ended Saturday sitting 19th in the table.

Sandro Tonali, the £100m midfielder from Newcastle, was overshadowed by Villa's tenacious skipper McGinn - a £2.75m buy from Hibs eight years ago.

Brazil winger Savio was denied three times by the impressive Suzuki but faded, while Omar Marmoush was signed to bring goals, but provided nothing.

De Zerbi said: "I didn't speak with the players [afterwards], I didn't want to say anything. The players who go to the national team, they have to play and work.

"The others, [James] Maddison, Gallagher, [Dominic] Solanke, Tosin [Adarabioyo], [Marcos] Senesi, Savio have to work more because their physical condition, I didn't like in this game."

Former Chelsea and England midfielder Joe Cole questioned Tottenham's transfer business after their spend of about £302m.

After Tonali, £85m went on bringing in Mateus Fernandes from West Ham. The Portuguese midfielder was subbed at half-time and De Zerbi said he "didn't like" Fernandes' performance, while £75m was spent on Savio from Manchester City.

Marmoush will cost £60m once his loan becomes permanent, but Spurs need their big-money buys to prove their worth and perform sooner rather than later.

"Spurs are dominant, chances, and you felt the tension growing - all of a sudden Spurs were just wanting to get to half-time. Once you defend with anxiety, things happen," Cole told TNT.

"When these things go against you, they go against you. Van de Ven going off was a factor, they didn't deal with it well. When you are anxious you make rash decisions.

"Villa defended well but didn't deserve to go in a goal up, and then this place deflated.

"They are not picking up points, a club flirting with relegation two years in a row, I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle."

De Zerbi, though, defended Tottenham's summer window spending despite their current malaise.

"I am happy with the squad, but the market was long, the situation changed many times," he said.

"There was also financial fair play and we have to respect that. We didn't sell the players we thought there was a possibility to sell.

"The club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players. If we didn't make any different decisions it was because we couldn't."

title: Suzuki proves worthy replacement for Martinez at Villa
description: Aston Villa new boy Zion Suzuki deserves as much credit as anyone for their first Premier League win of the season at struggling Tottenham.
fullText:
While Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson both scored, another Aston Villa new boy, Zion Suzuki, deserved as much credit as anyone for their first Premier League win of the season at struggling Tottenham.

The Japan goalkeeper made the move to Villa from Italian side Parma for a fee in the region of £30m in August.

And his performance against Spurs suggests he is more than capable of filling the very big boots vacated by the departure of Argentina number one - and fan favourite - Emiliano Martinez to Chelsea.

In particular, his two saves from Savio within seconds of each other and a moment of good fortune when Archie Gray's effort clipped wide off his foot, gave Villa the platform to ride out a period in the game when the hosts held sway.

"We needed the keeper," said Villa boss Unai Emery in his post-match interviews.

"He is a keeper to save us. To make sure in the goal he has the quality and then he has the skills to play and build up.

"It is very important how he is doing it and sometimes taking some risks, but through those he is improving and learning."

One of the attractions around signing the 24-year-old in August was his apparent assuredness with the ball at his feet and his ability to spray the ball forward with very little backlift.

And on a day when things could not have gone much better for him, Suzuki ended up as the architect of Villa's second goal, with his booming ball forward from his own six-yard box dropping deep into Tottenham territory, where Jackson collected it and dispatched an unerring shot to the left corner.

"In the build up, he can choose to play long balls because he has a very long pass in behind and he did that for the second goal we scored," added Emery.

Villa survive late Spurs fightback to earn first Premier League win

No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat

Born in the United States to a Ghanaian father and a Japanese mother, Suzuki has already played in Japan, Belgium and Italy and won 28 caps for his country.

And speaking to BBC Sport in August, Dennis Rudel - his former coach at Sint-Truiden - stressed that Suzuki has the attributes to become one of the world's best in his position.

"It is possible if he stays healthy," said the former Union Berlin coach. "With his physical strength, there is no-one better in the world in terms of dynamic, jumping power, throws and kicking the ball.

"When I watched him at the World Cup [for Japan], his biggest strength was his mental clearness. His focus on the game or in training sessions is so good. He is always prepared and really disciplined.

"He is aiming to show he can be one of the best. He was immediately one of the top four or five goalkeepers in Serie A.

"As a person and as a player, he is a role model for how you should behave. I don't see any weakness in him."

"He has such big hands and he is powerful. When he can reach the ball, it is a 90-95% chance of a save. It is something really special."

title: Villa's New Faces Come to the Fore as Emery's Side Finally Gets Off the Mark at Spurs
description: Dan Bardell reflects on Aston Villa's 3-2 victory at Tottenham, with Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Zion Suzuki among the new faces making their mark as Unai Emery's reshaped side finally secured the Premier League victory it desperately needed.
fullText:
Aston Villa win at Spurs, to get off the mark for the season in the Premier League.

Aston Villa needed a Premier League win at Tottenham Hotspur more than they needed a perfect performance, and while the final few minutes made a game that should have been comfortable far more uncomfortable than it needed to be, there was enough in the preceding 80 or so to suggest that some of the pieces of this new-look side are beginning to fall into place.

Going into the game, I wasn't particularly bothered how Villa got the three points. It had reached the stage where the result had to come first because another international break spent talking about a winless start to the Premier League season would have felt incredibly long, particularly after the disappointment of the Nottingham Forest defeat. Instead, Villa have gone to Tottenham, scored three times and won a game which contained enough encouraging individual performances to make the result feel like more than simply getting off the mark.

It certainly wasn't straightforward from the beginning. Spurs were the better side for periods of the first half and Villa needed Zion Suzuki, who was excellent, to make sure they stayed in the game when the home side had the momentum. There was a double save early on, another really good stop through a crowd of players and a general authority whenever the ball came into his penalty area which is becoming increasingly noticeable. Villa didn't control that opening period particularly well, but sometimes your goalkeeper has to get you through those moments and Suzuki did exactly that.

What Villa did have, even when they weren't controlling possession or creating chance after chance, was a threat in transition which gradually became more prominent as the game went on. Nicolas Jackson worked incredibly hard at the top end of the pitch and Johan Manzambi, making his first start, gave Villa something they have been missing. There were moments when the decision-making could have been better and occasions where the final ball wasn't quite there, but there was an athleticism and directness to Villa's attacking play which Tottenham increasingly struggled to deal with.

Manzambi's goal was scruffy in its construction, but I actually liked what it told us about him. He's playing as the number 10 but he wasn't standing on the edge of the penalty area admiring the situation; he had got himself into an area where he could sniff out a goal when the ball broke his way. For a 20-year-old making his first Premier League start, there was very little about him that looked tentative, and while I'll go into his performance in much more detail elsewhere, the most encouraging thing was how naturally he seemed to fit into the level of the game.

The second half was when Villa really started to look dangerous. Tottenham had to chase the game and inevitably left more space, but Villa still had to exploit it and for a period Jackson and Manzambi were causing them enormous problems. Jackson eventually got the goal his performance deserved, his first in the Premier League for Villa, and there were numerous examples before that of the qualities he gives this team. He can stretch a defence, he can run into the channels and he has that burst of acceleration which can turn a fairly innocuous situation into something dangerous very quickly. The relationship between him and Manzambi was particularly encouraging because Villa suddenly had two players capable of hurting Tottenham in different ways but operating in close enough proximity to combine.

Then Emi Buendía did what Emi Buendía does. I didn't think he had been particularly good in the first half and I've been critical of elements of his game this season, but I've also always said that he has the ability to produce a moment and his goal was exactly that. It was a brilliant strike and, once it went in, you could almost see the confidence flow through him. There is never really a question about his work rate or how much playing for Villa means to him, and even on an afternoon when everything hadn't come off with the ball, he still found a way to make a decisive contribution.

There were important performances at the other end as well. Tyrone Mings was very good for the majority of the afternoon and Villa needed that because this remains a team trying to establish a new hierarchy after so much change. Mings and John McGinn are incredibly important in that respect. There are younger players in the side, there are new players still learning exactly what Emery wants from them and there are others who may eventually develop into the organisers and leaders Villa need, but at this point those two are still fundamental to holding everything together. Mings dealt with so much of what came into the penalty area and I also thought some of his work in possession was excellent.

That is why the final stages were frustrating. At 3-0 the game should have been dead and Villa allowed Tottenham to make the scoreline far closer than it needed to be. The second goal in particular leaves a sour taste because game management has already been a talking point this season and there is clearly still work to do in terms of controlling matches when the momentum begins to change. The full-back areas were difficult for Villa for much of the afternoon as well, particularly in the first half, and this certainly wasn't a performance without flaws.

But those are things Villa can work on after a victory rather than spending another fortnight trying to explain why they haven't won a Premier League game. That distinction is important. This is a team which has undergone considerable change and there are combinations that are only beginning to develop, players still adapting to their surroundings and a manager working out exactly what his strongest version of this side looks like.

For the first time in the league this season, though, we saw enough of the upside to understand what that version might eventually become. Suzuki kept Villa in it when Tottenham were on top, Manzambi announced himself properly, Jackson gave Spurs problems throughout, Buendía produced the moment he is always capable of producing and the experience of players such as Mings and McGinn remained important around them.

The two late goals mean nobody should pretend everything has suddenly been solved, but Villa didn't need everything solved at Tottenham. They needed a win, they needed some of the new players to begin showing why they were brought to the football club and they needed something positive to take into the international break.

title: 'Fragile' Tottenham beaten by Aston Villa despite late rally
description: The end to Tottenham's Premier League goal drought came too late as Aston Villa won 3-2 in north London on Saturday to compound a miserable start for Roberto De Zerbi's men.Without a league win this season, Tottenham are off to their worst start in the Premier League era and only netted their first goals of the campaign after the visitors had surged into a 3-0 lead.
fullText:
The end to Tottenham's Premier League goal drought came too late as Aston Villa won 3-2 in north London on Saturday to compound a miserable start for Roberto De Zerbi's men.

Without a league win this season, Tottenham are off to their worst start in the Premier League era and only netted their first goals of the campaign after the visitors had surged into a 3-0 lead.

Villa had also struggled for goals themselves since the side that won the Europa League last season was torn apart during the transfer window.

But new signings Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson struck either side of half-time before Emi Buendia's wonder strike to give Unai Emery's new-look team their first league win.

"Competing like we did, winning like we did will give us confidence collectively and individually, it is really very important," said Emery.

"We are delighted because we needed it and we were suffering in the Premier League."

Even Tottenham's first late consolation needed the aid of a Villa deflection when Conor Gallagher's effort went in off Matty Cash before Jan Paul van Hecke headed home in stoppage time.

Spurs splashed out over £300 million ($400 million) on new players to try and avoid a repeat of the battle for survival they endured last season.

Yet there remains little return on that investment.

"I want to say is that we played well in the first half, we didn't score, but (we are ) too fragile," said De Zerbi.

"The moment when we have to defend, we have to defend compact. The leaders have to be leaders and to lead the team."

In keeping with recent performances, Spurs started brightly before fizzling out.

Twice in a matter of seconds Savio was kept out by Suzuki before the Japanese goalkeeper spread himself to turn behind Archie Gray's powerful strike.

Villa had picked up just one point from their opening four league games but have missed their club record signing Manzambi for most of that period.

The Swiss international opened his Villa account when he tapped home Boubacar Kamara's cross.

De Zerbi described Tottenham's defending for the second goal as "incredible" and not in a good sense as Van Hecke failed to deal with a long ball straight down the middle.

Jackson did well to evade the Dutch defender and then fired down into the ground and past Antonin Kinsky.

The Czech goalkeeper was powerless to stop Villa's third 11 minutes from time when Buendia took aim from long range and brilliantly picked out the top corner.

A chorus of boos greeted Buendia's strike as thousands of home fans headed for an early exit.

But those that left missed finally have something to celebrate.

Fine persistence from Mohammed Kudus teed up Gallagher to find the bottom corner via the outstretched foot of Cash.

Van Hecke then bulleted in from Andy Robertson's free-kick with virtually the last touch of the game.

Spurs now must stew on another defeat for a three-week international break while rooted in the relegation zone.

Villa, by contrast, will hope victory can prove the catalyst to storm up the table as they did last season.

Emery's men failed to win any of their first five league games a year ago, but ultimately finished fourth.

title: Winless Villa and Spurs face telling early showdown
description: Aston Villa and Tottenham are winless in the Premier League - and both in need of inspiration as they prepare to face each other on Saturday.
fullText:
More than half a billion spent between them, for just three points and one goal. Tottenham and Aston Villa are in need of Premier League inspiration.

It is not a surprise that a summer of change at both clubs has failed to bring immediate results - but they need to ignite their season.

They meet at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday as the past two Europa League winners but sitting in the bottom four of the early Premier League table.

With 10 new players, and six key sales - including Morgan Rogers and Ollie Watkins - Unai Emery is shaping a new Villa team.

Tottenham also added 10 players for more than £300m but goodwill is in short supply after two years of relegation battles. Victory is paramount for both teams.

At VIlla, Emery has credit in the bank after turning them from a team floundering in mid-table to Europa League winners - qualifying for Europe every season since his arrival, and getting them back into the Champions League this year.

This term there is a different remit, to be successful while integrating 10 new players - having spent more than £250m - following the summer exits.

Emery conceded he did not know exactly why Villa lost control during last Saturday's defeat by Nottingham Forest - but knows he was unable to make a significant impact from the touchline with all the new players still fitting in to their new set-up.

He can look frantic in his technical area during games, but has an impressive ability to decompress immediately and speak to the players calmly by the time he has returned to the dressing room.

Emery remains confident Villa will improve yet is relying on John McGinn and Tyrone Mings, as two of the senior players, to help him and the squad through a difficult patch.

It is a reason why both played in Wednesday's Carabao Cup win at Coventry rather than being rested.

Captain McGinn has previously described learning Emery's methods as doing "a lot of homework". That may be why Aaron Wan-Bissaka has struggled in his opening three games as he tries to adapt quickly - the same too for other new signings perhaps overthinking their roles.

An extended three-week break follows Saturday's match. But the head coach will not get the much-needed time on the training ground with his squad, as many go on international duty.

"This break is crazy because it's three weeks," Emery said. "I don't like to be three weeks but we must accept it.

"We are not going to have the players we want. [Johan] Manzambi played the first two matches with us and Saturday the third and then he goes with the national team.

"Back with us, we must again try to join him with us in our structure and his mind will maybe be confused.

"We don't want to use the international break as an excuse.

"Saturday is very important as we lack points but we continue in our process trying to work as well as possible."

Manzambi, brought in from Freiburg, and £47m winger Ibrahim Mbaye, who has moved from Paris St-Germain. made their debuts last weekend, coming off the bench against Forest, and are set to form part of a new attack.

Nicolas Jackson, signed from Chelsea in August, will start on Saturday after coming off the bench at the CBS Arena as Emery gets close to his preferred line-up, with Villa looking to click after notching just one point in their opening four games.

Only Villa, with 3.39, have a worse xG in the Premier League so far this season than Spurs' 3.45. Alysson's header in the 2-1 defeat by Forest was their first goal in the Premier League this term, with Spurs still searching for theirs.

Both are still worse than bottom club Coventry, who are pointless and goalless, but have an xG of 4.21.

Villa have had the lowest number of shots in the Premier League with 33, compared to Tottenham's 51, while their six on target is also the worst in the top flight followed by Spurs' 12.

Only Hull have had fewer touches in the box (47) than Villa's 62.

Yet Villa's defence must still be wary of struggling Spurs despite the hosts' lack of goals.

Matty Cash is available after recovering from a muscle problem but fellow defenders Pau Torres and Ian Maatsen are out for a match in which Villa can expect to face pressure. Only Manchester United, Arsenal, Brighton and Liverpool have made more passes in the final third than Tottenham (617), who have the highest successful pass completion rate, at 81.4%.

Villa's tally of 32 crosses, the lowest in the league, is half as many as Tottenham have managed.

It has been 407 minutes since Spurs last scored in the Premier League. They have failed to score in four successive Premier League matches - the first time that has happened since September 2006.

Their stalemate with Everton was their first goalless draw at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in the Premier League after 140 games.

But despite both sides' struggle for goals, history does not point to a 0-0 draw. None of the past 22 Premier League meetings between Spurs (15 wins) and Aston Villa (seven) have been drawn.

As Villa rebuild, they might hope a match against opponents struggling for wins might be the chance to kick-start their season. But they cannot afford to be lulled into a false sense of security.
